title: From noisy labels to intrinsic structure: A geometric-structural dual-guided framework for noise-robust medical image segmentation (GSD-Net)
mechanism: Geometric distance-aware pixel weights, structure-guided label refinement, and region swapping between image pairs for diversity.
adaptation: Distance weights from the crack distance transform down-weight the uncertain 1-2 px label edge. Region swaps pair cells from different sources. It is the most recent noise-robust baseline for the benchmark suite.
min_experiment: Arm: distance weights only (the cheapest component), 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if there is no detectable difference; run the full GSD-Net only for the benchmark.
evidence: R (web abstract): with simulated noise, +2.52% on Kvasir, +22.76% on Shenzhen, +8.87% on BU-SUC and +4.59% on BraTS2020; also tested on LIDC and MMIS-2024 with real multi-expert labels.

alt_notes.adaptation: Invert for cracks: down-weight background pixels 1 to 2 px from crack labels (likely true crack mislabelled as background) instead of crack boundary pixels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + distance-weighted CE near crack. Baseline: house. Metric: crack IoU and relR@2. Kill if crack IoU < house + 0.005. About 6 GPU-h.
